title: Apollo.io Review: AI Research, Agents and the Work Your Team Still Owns
summary: Apollo.io review of AI research, agent approvals, research credits and sequence behavior. See which tasks Apollo automates and which your team still owns.
body_markdown:
## Verdict: shortlist Apollo if someone owns the workflow


Apollo fits sales teams that want prospect data, research and outbound execution in the same workspace. For a VP of Sales or RevOps buyer, the decision is whether those connected tools match the way the team qualifies accounts, approves outreach and manages follow-up.


This review covers Apollo’s documentation and public pricing, checked November 10, 2026. We did not benchmark sending performance or contact-data accuracy in a live campaign.


The strongest reason to evaluate Apollo is the path from finding a prospect to researching fit and using that research in outreach. Its agents also perform scheduled work. The buying question is how much configuration and review your team is ready to own.


## What Apollo puts in one workspace


Apollo combines contact and account search, filters, enrichment, email sequences, calling, LinkedIn tasks, CRM integrations and reporting. AI research adds fields that can help qualify prospects or personalize messages.


Those fields can remain useful beyond the original research run. Apollo documents using research outputs to filter records, support further research and feed workflows. Decide whether a qualification answer needs to be a filterable category or a longer explanation before creating the field.


A research field can help determine who belongs in an audience; a sequence defines the outreach and tasks that follow. Agents can perform parts of that work, with operator decisions built into their documented flows.


## What agents do, and what your team still owns


Apollo’s agents can run daily, weekly or monthly, rather than only responding when someone opens the app. They are available on Professional and Organization plans through AI Assistant > Agents, with a configurable credit approval amount per run.


The[agent documentation](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/48316596060941-Use-Agents-to-Improve-Outbound-Work) describes distinct responsibilities:


Work


Apollo’s documented role


Your team’s role


Lead discovery


Finds ICP prospects, scores a sample and surfaces the strongest with rationale


Review and select leads to add to a list or sequence


Sequence creation


Recommends a target buyer, intent signal and sequence strategy


Choose the strategy, work through audience and setup, review the completed sequence and approve launch


Sequence optimization


Monitors opens, replies, bounces and spam signals; proposes one change at a time


Approve the change or refine it


AI research fields


Runs templates or custom prompts and stores outputs


Define context and model, inspect answers, and review, edit or regenerate results


Sequence execution


Sends automated emails and organizes manual steps


Configure sending and rules, complete manual tasks and manage overlapping outreach


Assign a named reviewer before enabling scheduled runs so recommendations have an owner. During the trial, measure the work that person does between receiving a recommendation and approving the next action.


## From research question to sequence enrollment


Start with one qualification decision your team already makes. Apollo’s[research setup guide](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/29436100461837-Use-AI-Research-to-Qualify-and-Understand-Prospects) gives this example: “Determine if these accounts have the necessary technical skills to implement a new CRM.”


Follow the documented workflow to evaluate how Apollo answers that kind of question:


1.


Configure the AI context center with information about your products or services.


2.


Open People or Companies, filter the audience and choose Research with AI.


3.


Select a template or write a custom prompt. Assisted custom mode accepts a natural-language goal and lets you preview results and edit the prompt.


4.


Choose the context, model and output field. Apollo supports single-line, multi-line and single-select fields.


5.


Preview answers, inspect them, then save and run on the first 10 or 25 rows, or save without running. Selection limits depend on the plan.


6.


Review the resulting fields before using them to filter an audience or personalize messages, then enroll contacts through the chosen sequence workflow.


Apollo allows up to three free previews per prompt. Use them to check whether the question is specific enough and whether an unknown answer stays unknown. The field type cannot change after creation, so decide how the team will use the output before saving. Global fields require permission to add or edit custom-field definitions.


Model choice determines what evidence research can reach. According to the[AI Research Overview](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/29193277882125-AI-Research-Overview) , GPT-4o mini categorizes and summarizes Apollo data without web access. Perplexity Agent has web access and may miss paywalled material. Check the model before treating an answer as current web research.


Changes to AI context affect future research only. Existing answers require a rerun. Include that rerun in the operating process when a qualification rule changes, so a saved field does not retain an older interpretation.


## Credit and seat economics


Budget for research by output column, alongside the seat price. Apollo’s[public pricing](https://www.apollo.io/pricing) , checked November 10, 2026, lists:


Plan


Price per seat/month, billed annually


Included credits per seat/year


Sequence allowance


Free


$0


900, granted monthly


Two sequences


Basic


$49


30,000, granted upfront


Unlimited sequences


Professional


$79


48,000, granted upfront


Unlimited sequences and A/Z testing


Organization


$119, minimum three seats


72,000, granted upfront


Unlimited sequences and A/Z testing


Agent access is a separate plan consideration: the agent documentation specifies Professional and Organization.


For AI research fields, the documented charge is one credit per record per output column. Apollo’s own example is ten contacts researched across three columns for thirty credits. The pricing page’s “AI research: 1 credit per run” does not mean one credit researches an entire audience across every field.


Public pricing also lists email access at one credit, phone-number access at eight, and enrichment at one to eight. Connected AI-tool research using Google Maps, directories or web search may have different costs; the tool quotes the cost and asks for approval.


Review the[credit usage report](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/9527776320781-Review-Credit-Usage-in-Apollo) during evaluation. It groups research, enrichment, phones, email, infrastructure and, for some plans or legacy configurations, exports. Do not assume every export is charged. Set per-user credit limits and workflow processing limits before expanding research.


## Sequences still include manual work


Apollo sequences combine automated email with manual email, phone calls, LinkedIn actions and other tasks. A sequence can coordinate a rep’s work without automatically performing every step.


The[sequence documentation](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409237165837-Sequences-Overview) describes connecting a mailbox, creating and activating a sequence, enrolling contacts and reviewing warnings. Enrollment can come from search, lists, CSV uploads, profiles or workflows.


Inspect the ruleset before sending. Apollo can stop a contact after a reply or keep that contact enrolled, depending on the rules. Confirm the intended behavior rather than assuming every reply ends outreach.


Also check what happens when a rep contacts someone outside the sequence. A direct email or call from a profile does not replace scheduled messages while the contact remains enrolled. Pause or remove the contact when needed to avoid overlap. Apollo’s multiple-sequence enrollment warning can be overridden; the contact then receives messages from all enrolled sequences.


Reps need to know when to complete a task, pause outreach or remove a contact, while RevOps needs to own the rules and warnings.


## Who should trial Apollo, and what to check


Apollo belongs on the shortlist when the team wants combined data and execution and can name an owner for configuration, research review and campaign approval. A small team can benefit from that consolidation too. Free access, however, cannot evaluate the paid agents and allows only two sequences.


Make the trial answer operational questions rather than only demonstrating that research produces text:


-


Inspect contact records for current employment, relevant job role and actual account fit.


-


Match the chosen research model’s source access to the question. Check the evidence supporting answers.


-


Review positive and unknown outputs separately. Ask whether a positive answer has support, rather than rewarding a filled field.


-


Change the AI context and verify the process for rerunning existing fields.


-


Check per-user credit limits and the report after research runs.


-


Review mailbox sending settings, reply rules and multiple-sequence warnings before enrollment.


-


Confirm CRM field mapping so the intended research and qualification information reaches the correct fields.


Record who makes each decision and how much interpretation the research output needs before a contact is ready for outreach.


## FAQ


### Can Apollo qualify prospects automatically?


Apollo documents AI research for qualification and an agent that discovers ICP prospects, scores a sample and presents the strongest leads with rationale. In that agent flow, the operator reviews and selects leads for a list or sequence. Evaluate the qualification output and the selection step together.


### Does research need a custom field before it can personalize an email?


Apollo’s built-in research workflow stores outputs in fields that can personalize messages. Its[connected Claude or ChatGPT email workflow](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409237165837-Sequences-Overview) is distinct: personalized emails can be generated and applied without custom fields after review and approval. Choose the workflow based on whether the answer also needs to support filtering or later research.


### Does Apollo automate LinkedIn messages in sequences?


Apollo’s sequence overview lists LinkedIn actions among the manual steps, alongside calls and manual emails. Include the rep’s task-completion time when evaluating a sequence that uses LinkedIn.


### Can Apollo’s optimization agent change a campaign without review?


The documented optimization flow proposes one change at a time for the operator to approve or refine. During a trial, inspect the proposed change and decide who has authority to accept it before enabling recurring optimization.
